records.source: וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] eleventh year, on [the] first of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: In the eleventh year, on the first day of a month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: And it came about in the eleventh year, on the first of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.1: On the first day of a month in the eleventh year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the eleventh year, on the first of the month: 587 or 586 BC, the year Jerusalem fell; the month is not named
decisions.reason: Ezekiel counts the years from King Jehoiachin's exile in 597 BC (1:2). The eleventh year ran from the spring of 587 BC to the spring of 586 BC, and Jerusalem fell in that year (Jeremiah 39:2; 52:5-6). The Hebrew gives the day but not the month. Since Tyre is already gloating over Jerusalem's ruin (verse 2), the oracle probably came late in the year, but a number may have dropped out of the text.

decisions.choice: Tyre: the great Phoenician port, the subject of 26:1-28:19
decisions.reason: Tyre stood on a small island about half a mile off the coast of what is now Lebanon, with towns on the mainland opposite. It was the leading trading city of the eastern Mediterranean. Its king Hiram supplied cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and Solomon's temple (2 Samuel 5:11; 1 Kings 5:15-32). Three chapters are given to it: an oracle of destruction (26), a lament over Tyre as a great ship (27), and words to its ruler (28:1-19).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: Tyre will become a bare rock

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר־אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, because that said Tyre concerning Jerusalem, Aha! Broken [are the] doors of the peoples; it has turned to me; I will be filled, she is laid waste,
pieces: Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, "Aha! The gateway of the nations is broken, and its doors have swung open to me. She lies in ruins, and I will grow rich,"

L.2: Son of man, because Tyre has said about Jerusalem, "Aha! Broken [are] the doors of the peoples; it has swung open to me; I will be filled, [now that] she is laid waste,"

R.2: Son of man, the people of Tyre laughed at Jerusalem and said, "Aha! The city that was the gateway for the nations is broken down. Its doors are open to me now. Jerusalem is ruined, so I will get rich."

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: the doors of the peoples: Jerusalem as a gateway of trade between the nations
alternatives: the city the peoples came to
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood on the inland routes between Egypt, Arabia and the north, and could control and tax the trade that passed. With it broken, Tyre expects the traffic and the profit to come its way. The words may also picture Jerusalem as the city to which the peoples came.

decisions.choice: Aha!: a cry of gloating
decisions.reason: Tyre gloats as Ammon did (25:3). It sees a rival's ruin as a business opportunity.

decisions.choice: I will be filled: I will grow rich
decisions.reason: Tyre expects to be filled with goods and wealth. The theme of its wealth runs through chapters 26-28.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for Tyre's words
decisions.reason: Speech quoted inside the LORD's oracle takes double quotes. Balanced and Readable say "grow rich" for "be filled", and Readable names Jerusalem as the city that is ruined.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ צֹ֑ר וְהַעֲלֵיתִ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים כְּהַעֲל֥וֹת הַיָּ֖ם לְגַלָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] against you, Tyre, and I will bring up against you many nations, as brings up the sea its waves.
pieces: therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations against you, as the sea hurls up its waves.

L.3: therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, Tyre, and I will bring up many nations against you, even as the sea makes its waves rise.

R.3: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Tyre, I am against you. I will bring many nations to attack you. They will come against you like the waves of the sea.

decisions.choice: I am against you: the LORD declares himself Tyre's enemy
decisions.reason: The words announce the LORD's hostility, as against Jerusalem (5:8) and the false prophets (13:8).

decisions.choice: as the sea brings up its waves: the sea that made Tyre great will bring its attackers
decisions.reason: Tyre lived by the sea and on it. Now the nations will come against it wave after wave, like the sea against its rock.

decisions.choice: many nations: the armies that will come against Tyre
decisions.reason: Babylon's army drew troops from many peoples (verse 7). The words also leave room for more than one attacker over time.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.source: וְשִׁחֲת֞וּ חֹמ֣וֹת צֹ֗ר וְהָֽרְסוּ֙ מִגְדָּלֶ֔יהָ וְסִֽחֵיתִ֥י עֲפָרָ֖הּ מִמֶּ֑נָּה וְנָתַתִּ֥י אוֹתָ֖הּ לִצְחִ֥יחַ סָֽלַע׃
records.gloss: And they will destroy [the] walls of Tyre and break down her towers, and I will scrape her dust from her and make her a bare rock.
pieces: They will destroy the walls of Tyre and pull down her towers. I will scrape away her rubble and make her a bare rock.

L.4: And they will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers, and I will scrape her dust from her and make her a bare rock.

R.4: They will knock down the walls of Tyre and destroy its towers. I will scrape away even its soil and leave nothing but bare rock.

decisions.choice: a bare rock: a play on the name Tyre
decisions.reason: The name Tyre means "rock". The city built on a rock will be scraped down to the bare rock itself.

decisions.choice: her dust: the soil and rubble of the city
decisions.reason: Even the earth on the island will be scraped away, so that nothing is left to build on.

decisions.choice: its (R); her (L, B)
decisions.reason: Hebrew speaks of cities as "she". Literal and Balanced keep "she" and "her" for Tyre, as in Isaiah 23; Readable says "it", so that young readers do not take the city for a woman.

records.source: מִשְׁטַ֨ח חֲרָמִ֤ים תִּֽהְיֶה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיָּ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהָיְתָ֥ה לְבַ֖ז לַגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: A spreading place of nets it will be in [the] midst of the sea, for I have spoken, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh, and it will become plunder for [the] nations.
pieces: Out in the sea she will become a place where nets are spread to dry, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. She will become the nations' plunder.

L.5: A place for spreading nets she will be in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; and she will become plunder for the nations.

R.5: It will be a place out in the sea where fishermen spread out their nets to dry. I have spoken, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. The nations will take everything Tyre owns.

decisions.choice: a place for spreading nets: a bare rock used by fishermen
decisions.reason: Fishermen spread their nets on flat rocks to dry and mend them (47:10). The proud city will be nothing more than that.

decisions.choice: in the midst of the sea: Tyre's island
decisions.reason: The city stood on an island off the coast, which made it hard to take (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: to dry (B, R); fishermen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why nets are spread on a rock.

records.source: וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And her daughters who [are] in the field by sword will be killed, and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Her daughter towns on the mainland will be put to the sword. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: And her daughters who [are] in the field will be killed by the sword, and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: The people in the towns that belong to Tyre on the mainland will be killed in war. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: her daughters who are in the field: the towns on the mainland that belonged to Tyre
decisions.reason: Hebrew calls the towns that depend on a city its "daughters" (Jeremiah 49:2). "The field" is the open country, here the mainland opposite the island.

decisions.choice: daughter towns on the mainland (B); the towns that belong to Tyre on the mainland (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל־צֹ֗ר נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מְלָכִ֑ים בְּס֛וּס וּבְרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים וְקָהָ֥ל וְעַם־רָֽב׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] about to bring against Tyre Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, from [the] north, king of kings, with horses and with chariots and with horsemen, and a company and a people numerous.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am bringing against Tyre from the north Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses, chariots and horsemen, a great horde of troops.

L.7: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am bringing against Tyre from the north Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and with chariotry and with horsemen, and a company, and a people great [in number].

R.7: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, the greatest king of all, to attack Tyre from the north. He will come with horses, chariots and horsemen and a huge army.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon: the same king as Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: He ruled Babylon from 605 to 562 BC. Ezekiel spells his name with an r, closer to the Babylonian form, as Jeremiah usually does (see Jeremiah 21:2). It is one man either way.

decisions.choice: king of kings: the title of the great emperors
decisions.reason: The kings of Mesopotamia and Persia called themselves "king of kings", since lesser kings served them (Ezra 7:12; Daniel 2:37).

decisions.choice: from the north: the way invaders came
decisions.reason: Babylon lies east of Tyre across the desert, but its armies came by the road along the Euphrates and down from the north, as Jeremiah says (Jeremiah 1:14; 4:6).

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar's siege of Tyre
decisions.reason: Nebuchadrezzar besieged Tyre for thirteen years, from about 585 to 572 BC, according to the Jewish historian Josephus (stated from general knowledge). Tyre submitted to Babylon, but the island city was not plundered, as Ezekiel himself says in 29:17-20.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the spelling the Hebrew of Ezekiel uses. Readable says "the greatest king of all" for "king of kings".

records.heading: Nebuchadrezzar against Tyre

records.source: בְּנוֹתַ֥יִךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה בַּחֶ֣רֶב יַהֲרֹ֑ג וְנָתַ֨ן עָלַ֜יִךְ דָּיֵ֗ק וְשָׁפַ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ סֹֽלְלָ֔ה וְהֵקִ֥ים עָלַ֖יִךְ צִנָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Your daughters in the field with the sword he will kill, and he will set against you a siege wall, and he will pour out against you a ramp, and he will raise against you a shield.
pieces: He will put your daughter towns on the mainland to the sword. He will build a siege wall against you, heap up a ramp against you and raise his shields against you.

L.8: Your daughters in the field he will kill with the sword, and he will set up a siege wall against you, and pour out a ramp against you, and raise a shield against you.

R.8: He will kill the people in your towns on the mainland. He will build siege walls around you and pile up dirt ramps against your walls. His soldiers will hold up their shields as they attack you.

decisions.choice: a siege wall, a ramp and a shield: the works of a siege
decisions.reason: An army built a wall or towers around a city, heaped up earth into ramps to bring its battering rams to the walls, and moved forward under large shields (4:2; 21:27; 2 Kings 25:1).

decisions.choice: your daughters: the oracle now speaks to Tyre directly
decisions.reason: Verse 6 spoke of "her daughters"; now the LORD addresses the city as "you".

decisions.choice: raise his shields (B); his soldiers will hold up their shields (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the large shield that covered a soldier's whole body. Balanced and Readable make clear that it is the attackers' shield.

records.source: וּמְחִ֣י קָֽבָלּ֔וֹ יִתֵּ֖ן בְּחֹֽמוֹתָ֑יִךְ וּמִ֨גְדְּלֹתַ֔יִךְ יִתֹּ֖ץ בְּחַרְבוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And the blow of his battering ram he will set against your walls, and your towers he will break down with his swords.
pieces: He will aim the blows of his battering rams at your walls and tear down your towers with his iron tools.

L.9: And the blow of his battering ram he will set against your walls, and your towers he will break down with his swords.

R.9: He will pound your walls with battering rams. He will tear down your towers with iron tools.

decisions.choice: the blow of his battering ram
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. The first means a striking; the second is probably a battering ram, a heavy beam swung against a wall or gate.

decisions.choice: his swords: iron tools for breaking down walls
decisions.reason: The word for "sword" is also used of other iron tools, such as a chisel (Exodus 20:25). Towers are broken down with picks and axes.

decisions.choice: iron tools
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "swords" are used for here (m2). Literal keeps "swords".

records.source: מִשִּׁפְעַ֥ת סוּסָ֖יו יְכַסֵּ֣ךְ אֲבָקָ֑ם מִקּוֹל֩ פָּרַ֨שׁ וְגַלְגַּ֜ל וָרֶ֗כֶב תִּרְעַ֨שְׁנָה֙ חֽוֹמוֹתַ֔יִךְ בְּבֹאוֹ֙ בִּשְׁעָרַ֔יִךְ כִּמְבוֹאֵ֖י עִ֥יר מְבֻקָּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: From [the] abundance of his horses their dust will cover you; from [the] sound of horseman and wheel and chariot your walls will shake, when he enters your gates as [men] enter a city broken into.
pieces: His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you. The noise of horsemen, wheels and chariots will make your walls shake when he comes through your gates, as troops pour into a city whose walls are breached.

L.10: From the abundance of his horses their dust will cover you; at the sound of horsemen and wheels and chariots your walls will shake, when he enters your gates as [men] enter a city broken open.

R.10: He will have so many horses that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake from the noise of the horsemen, the wheels and the chariots when he comes in through your gates, the way soldiers rush into a city after its walls are broken down.

decisions.choice: as men enter a city broken open: as an army storms a city through a breach
decisions.reason: Once the wall is breached, soldiers pour in. The picture is of a city taken by storm.

decisions.choice: horses, chariots and gates: the usual picture of a city taken by land
decisions.reason: The oracle uses the language of a siege on land. Babylon could take the mainland towns this way; the island city could be reached by land only across a causeway, which was built centuries later (see verse 12).

decisions.choice: as troops pour into a city whose walls are breached (B); the way soldiers rush into (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who enters, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

records.source: בְּפַרְס֣וֹת סוּסָ֔יו יִרְמֹ֖ס אֶת־כָּל־חֽוּצוֹתָ֑יִךְ עַמֵּךְ֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יַהֲרֹ֔ג וּמַצְּב֥וֹת עֻזֵּ֖ךְ לָאָ֥רֶץ תֵּרֵֽד׃
records.gloss: With [the] hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; your people with the sword he will kill, and [the] pillars of your strength to the ground will go down.
pieces: His horses' hooves will trample every street you have. He will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will crash to the ground.

L.11: With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; your people he will kill with the sword, and the pillars of your strength will go down to the ground.

R.11: His horses will trample all your streets. He will kill your people in battle, and your great stone pillars will fall to the ground.

decisions.choice: the pillars of your strength: Tyre's great standing pillars
alternatives: the strong pillars of the city's buildings
decisions.reason: The word is used of standing stones set up for worship. It may mean the famous pillars of Tyre's temple of its god Melqart, which the Greek historian Herodotus describes (stated from general knowledge), or the strong pillars of the city's buildings.

decisions.choice: in battle
decisions.reason: Readable says "in battle" for "with the sword", as it does in 17:21.

records.source: וְשָׁלְל֣וּ חֵילֵ֗ךְ וּבָֽזְזוּ֙ רְכֻלָּתֵ֔ךְ וְהָֽרְסוּ֙ חוֹמוֹתַ֔יִךְ וּבָתֵּ֥י חֶמְדָּתֵ֖ךְ יִתֹּ֑צוּ וַאֲבָנַ֤יִךְ וְעֵצַ֨יִךְ֙ וַֽעֲפָרֵ֔ךְ בְּת֥וֹךְ מַ֖יִם יָשִֽׂימוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will plunder your wealth and they will take as spoil your merchandise, and they will tear down your walls and your houses of delight they will pull down, and your stones and your timbers and your dust in [the] midst of [the] waters they will put.
pieces: They will plunder your wealth and seize your goods. They will tear down your walls and demolish your fine houses, and they will throw your stones, timber and rubble into the sea.

L.12: And they will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise, and they will tear down your walls and pull down your pleasant houses, and your stones and your timbers and your dust they will put in the midst of the waters.

R.12: Your enemies will steal your riches and take away the goods you sell. They will knock down your walls and destroy your beautiful houses. They will throw the stones, the wood and even the dirt into the sea.

decisions.choice: they: the attackers in general
decisions.reason: Verses 7-11 speak of "he", Nebuchadrezzar; now the verbs are plural. "They" may be his troops, or the "many nations" of verse 3, coming over time like waves.

decisions.choice: your merchandise: the goods Tyre traded
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb for going about as a trader. The wealth of Tyre's trade is the theme of chapter 27 and of 28:5, 16, 18.

decisions.choice: stones, timber and soil thrown into the water
decisions.reason: The ruins are dumped into the sea. In 332 BC Alexander the Great took the island city by building a causeway out to it from the mainland, using the rubble of the old town (stated from general knowledge). Many readers have seen this verse in that event; the text names no attacker after Nebuchadrezzar.

decisions.choice: Your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are (m1).

records.source: וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֖י הֲמ֣וֹן שִׁירָ֑יִךְ וְק֣וֹל כִּנּוֹרַ֔יִךְ לֹ֥א יִשָּׁמַ֖ע עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And I will put an end to [the] noise of your songs, and [the] sound of your lyres will not be heard again.
pieces: I will silence the noise of your songs, and the music of your lyres will never be heard again.

L.13: And I will put an end to the noise of your songs, and the sound of your lyres will not be heard again.

R.13: I will stop your noisy singing. No one will ever hear the music of your harps again.

decisions.choice: the end of songs and music: the end of a city's life
decisions.reason: When a city falls, its feasts and celebrations stop (Isaiah 24:8; Jeremiah 7:34; Amos 5:23). Isaiah 23:16 pictures Tyre with a lyre in her hand.

decisions.choice: lyres (L, B); harps (R)
decisions.reason: The instrument is a small stringed lyre. Readable says "harps", a word young readers know for a plucked instrument.

records.source: וּנְתַתִּ֞יךְ לִצְחִ֣יחַ סֶ֗לַע מִשְׁטַ֤ח חֲרָמִים֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבָּנֶ֖ה ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will make you bare rock; a spreading place of nets you will be; you will not be built again, for I, Yahweh, have spoken, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: I will make you a bare rock, a place for spreading nets. You will never be built again, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And I will make you a bare rock; a place for spreading nets you will be; you will not be built again, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: I will make you a bare rock where fishermen dry their nets. No one will ever build you again. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have said it, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: bare rock, a place for spreading nets: the words of verses 4-5 again
decisions.reason: The first oracle on Tyre ends as it began, with the city scraped down to the rock it was named for.

decisions.choice: you will not be built again: the end of Tyre as it was
decisions.reason: A town called Tyre stood on the site again in later centuries and is there today (Acts 21:3). The oracle speaks in the strong language prophets use for total ruin, and the proud island city of Ezekiel's day, rich and independent, did not return. Ezekiel himself later says that Nebuchadrezzar's army gained nothing from Tyre (29:17-20), which shows that the book did not hide how events turned out.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה לְצ֑וֹר הֲלֹ֣א׀מִקּ֣וֹל מַפַּלְתֵּ֗ךְ בֶּאֱנֹ֨ק חָלָ֜ל בֵּהָ֤רֵֽג הֶ֨רֶג֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֔ךְ יִרְעֲשׁ֖וּ הָאִיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to Tyre: Not from [the] sound of your downfall, when groan [the] wounded, when is killed a slaughter in your midst, will quake the coastlands?
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and the killing goes on within you?

L.15: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to Tyre: At the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan, when slaughter is done in your midst, will not the coastlands quake?

R.15: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to Tyre: The lands far away across the sea will shake with fear at the noise of your fall, when your wounded groan and many are killed in your streets.

decisions.choice: the coastlands: the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The word means coasts and islands, the lands across the sea with which Tyre traded (27:3, 6-7, 15, 35).

decisions.choice: will not the coastlands quake?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying that they certainly will.

decisions.choice: the lands far away across the sea
decisions.reason: Readable follows the Isaiah table for *iyyim* ("lands far away") and gives the question as a statement (m2).

records.heading: The princes of the sea mourn

records.source: וְֽיָרְד֞וּ מֵעַ֣ל כִּסְאוֹתָ֗ם כֹּ֚ל נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הַיָּ֔ם וְהֵסִ֨ירוּ֙ אֶת־מְעִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־בִּגְדֵ֥י רִקְמָתָ֖ם יִפְשֹׁ֑טוּ חֲרָד֤וֹת׀יִלְבָּ֨שׁוּ֙ עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ יֵשֵׁ֔בוּ וְחָֽרְדוּ֙ לִרְגָעִ֔ים וְשָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And will go down from on their thrones all [the] princes of the sea, and they will remove their robes, and their garments of embroidery they will strip off; [with] trembling they will be clothed; on the ground they will sit, and they will tremble every moment and be appalled over you.
pieces: All the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes and strip off their embroidered clothes. Trembling will be their clothing. They will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at your fate.

L.16: And all the princes of the sea will go down from their thrones and remove their robes, and their embroidered garments they will strip off; [with] trembling they will clothe themselves; on the ground they will sit, and they will tremble every moment and be appalled over you.

R.16: All the rulers of the cities by the sea will get down from their thrones. They will take off their royal robes and their colorful clothes. They will be so afraid that they shake all over. They will sit on the ground and shake with fear all the time. They will be horrified at what happened to you.

decisions.choice: the princes of the sea: the rulers of the coastal and island cities
decisions.reason: The word is *nasi'*, a ruler or chief. These are the rulers of the trading cities that depended on Tyre.

decisions.choice: down from their thrones, robes removed, sitting on the ground: the actions of mourning
decisions.reason: Mourners took off fine clothing and sat on the ground (Job 2:12-13; Jonah 3:6). The rulers act as if at a funeral.

decisions.choice: they will clothe themselves with trembling: fear will cover them like clothing
decisions.reason: The fine robes come off, and fear takes their place (compare 7:27).

decisions.choice: princes (L, B); rulers (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *nasi'* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֣יךְ אָבַ֔דְתְּ נוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת מִיַּמִּ֑ים הָעִ֣יר הַהֻלָּ֗לָה אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיְתָ֨ה חֲזָקָ֤ה בַיָּם֙ הִ֣יא וְיֹשְׁבֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּיתָ֖ם לְכָל־יוֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And they will take up over you a lament and say to you: How you have perished, [you] inhabited from [the] seas, the city renowned, which was mighty in the sea, she and her inhabitants, who put their terror on all her inhabitants!
pieces: They will raise a lament over you and say to you, \q "How you have perished, you who were peopled from the seas, \q the renowned city that was mighty on the sea, she and those who lived in her, \q who spread their terror over all who lived there!

L.17: And they will raise a lament over you and say to you, \q "How you have perished, [you who were] inhabited from the seas, \q the renowned city, which was mighty on the sea, she and her inhabitants, \q who laid their terror on all her inhabitants!

R.17: They will sing a funeral song about you. They will say, \q "How you have been destroyed, city of sailors! \q You were famous and powerful on the sea, you and your people. \q Everyone who lived around you was afraid of you.

decisions.choice: a lament: a funeral song, here sung by the rulers of the sea
decisions.reason: See the note at 19:1. The lament begins with "How", as funeral songs do (2 Samuel 1:19; Lamentations 1:1). Verses 17-18 are set in lines as poetry.

decisions.choice: inhabited from the seas: a city peopled by seafarers
alternatives: you who rose from the seas
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that Tyre drew its people from the sea, a city of sailors and traders, or that it rose up out of the sea. The words are unusual.

decisions.choice: who laid their terror on all her inhabitants: Tyre made everyone fear it
alternatives: on all who lived by the sea
decisions.reason: The last line is hard. It may mean that Tyre and its people were feared by all who lived on the sea, or by all who lived in its sphere of power.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the lament, and lines
decisions.reason: The lament is sung by the rulers of the sea, so it is human speech quoted in the oracle and takes double quotes, which close at the end of verse 18. The verses follow the Hebrew accents for their line breaks. Readable says "funeral song" for *qinah*, as in 19:1.

decisions.choice: city of sailors
alternatives: you who were peopled from the seas
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likeliest sense of "inhabited from the seas" (m2).

records.source: עַתָּה֙ יֶחְרְד֣וּ הָֽאִיִּ֔ן י֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּ֑ךְ וְנִבְהֲל֛וּ הָאִיִּ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בַּיָּ֖ם מִצֵּאתֵֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Now tremble the coastlands [the] day of your downfall, and are terrified the coastlands which [are] in the sea at your going out.
pieces: Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall, \q and the islands of the sea are dismayed at your passing."

L.18: Now the coastlands tremble [on the] day of your downfall, \q and the coastlands that [are] in the sea are terrified at your departure."

R.18: Now the lands far away tremble on the day of your fall. \q The islands in the sea are terrified because you are gone."

decisions.choice: your departure: your going out of the world, your end
alternatives: the going out of your people into exile
decisions.reason: The word means a going out. Here it most likely means Tyre's passing away, its death, parallel to "your downfall".

decisions.choice: the coastlands ... the coastlands: one word, in two spellings
decisions.reason: The first has an unusual ending, the second the usual one. The repetition frames the verse.

decisions.choice: the islands of the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the repeated word with "islands", which is part of its sense; Literal keeps "coastlands" twice.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּתִתִּ֤י אֹתָךְ֙ עִ֣יר נֶחֱרֶ֔בֶת כֶּעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־נוֹשָׁ֑בוּ בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ אֶת־תְּה֔וֹם וְכִסּ֖וּךְ הַמַּ֥יִם הָרַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: When I make you a city desolate, like cities which are not inhabited, when I bring up over you the deep, and cover you the waters many,
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: When I make you a desolate city, like cities where no one lives, when I bring the deep up over you and its vast waters cover you,

L.19: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: When I make you a ruined city, like cities that have no inhabitants, when I bring up the deep over you, and the many waters cover you,

R.19: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will make you a city in ruins, like other cities where no one lives. I will bring the deep sea over you, and its great waters will cover you.

decisions.choice: the deep: the great ocean beneath and around the world
decisions.reason: The deep is the vast water of creation and of the flood (Genesis 1:2; 7:11). The sea that made Tyre rich will swallow it.

decisions.choice: when ... when ...: the sentence goes on into verse 20
decisions.reason: Verse 19 sets the time; verse 20 says what the LORD will then do.

records.heading: Down to the pit

records.source: וְהוֹרַדְתִּיךְ֩ אֶת־י֨וֹרְדֵי ב֜וֹר אֶל־עַ֣ם עוֹלָ֗ם וְ֠הוֹשַׁבְתִּיךְ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ תַּחְתִּיּ֜וֹת כָּחֳרָב֤וֹת מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ אֶת־י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֔וֹר לְמַ֖עַן לֹ֣א תֵשֵׁ֑בִי וְנָתַתִּ֥י צְבִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: and I will bring you down with [those who] go down [to the] pit, to [the] people of antiquity, and I will make you dwell in [the] land of [the] lowest parts, like ruins from antiquity, with [those who] go down [to the] pit, so that not you will be inhabited; and I will put splendor in [the] land of [the] living.
pieces: then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the world below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will no longer be inhabited. But I will give splendor to the land of the living.

L.20: then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago, and I will make you dwell in the land of the depths, like the ruins of long ago, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I will set splendor in the land of the living.

R.20: Then I will send you down to the pit, the world of the dead. You will join the people who died long ago. I will make you live in the world deep below, like ruins from long ago, with all who have gone down to the pit. No one will live in you again. But I will make the land of the living beautiful.

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave, the world of the dead
decisions.reason: The word means a cistern or pit and is used of the grave and of Sheol (Isaiah 14:15; Psalm 28:1). "Those who go down to the pit" are the dead. The phrase returns in Ezekiel's laments over the king of Tyre (28:8) and over Egypt (31:14-18; 32:18-30).

decisions.choice: the land of the depths: the underworld
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the world of the dead as lying deep below the earth (31:14, 16, 18; 32:18, 24).

decisions.choice: and I will set splendor in the land of the living
alternatives: so that you will not ... stand in the land of the living
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. As it stands it sets the LORD's gift of splendor to the land of the living, perhaps his own land, against Tyre's descent to the dead. The Greek translation reads "nor stand" instead of "and I will set splendor", giving "so that you will not be inhabited or have a place in the land of the living" (stated from general knowledge); that needs a change of one letter and of the vowels. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: the pit, at every level
decisions.reason: "The pit" stays at every level, as in Isaiah 14:15; Readable adds "the world of the dead" the first time it appears.

records.source: בַּלָּה֥וֹת אֶתְּנֵ֖ךְ וְאֵינֵ֑ךְ וּֽתְבֻקְשִׁ֗י וְלֹֽא־תִמָּצְאִ֥י עוֹד֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Sudden terrors I will make you, and you will not [be]; and you will be sought, and not you will be found again forever, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: I will bring you to a terrifying end, and you will be no more. People will look for you, but you will never be found again, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: Sudden terrors I will make you, and you will be no more; and you will be sought, but you will not be found again forever, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: I will bring you to a horrible end, and you will be gone. People will look for you, but they will never find you again, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: sudden terrors I will make you: I will bring you to a dreadful end
alternatives: I will make you a horror
decisions.reason: The word means sudden terror or a dreadful end (Job 18:11, 14). "I will make you terrors" may mean that Tyre will become an object of horror to others, or that terrors will overtake it.

decisions.choice: the refrain that closes the Tyre oracles
decisions.reason: The same words end the lament over Tyre (27:36) and the lament over its king (28:19).

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.
